heroHeadline: VP Lara releases a second Cerimedo audio and sues the First Lady as Santa Cruz blockades partly lift and cocaleros march in Cochabamba
heroSubtitle: Vice President Edmand Lara escalated his break with President Paz, filing a Sept. 1 criminal complaint against First Lady María Elena Urquidi and Fernando Cerimedo over the ouster of Police Commander Mirko Sokol (who resigned Aug. 31 amid a separate audio-leak corruption probe), then releasing a second disputed audio on Sept. 3 alleging Paz and Cerimedo scripted a "narrative" for the June 20 state-of-exception decree — claims Paz declined to confirm or deny pending forensic review. Separately, San Julián and Cuatro Cañadas lifted their diesel-decree blockades Sept. 3 after the government's Decree 5698 raised the subsidized-diesel cap for small producers, though Yapacaní's blockade held and thousands of Morales-aligned cocaleros marched into Cochabamba on Sept. 4 defying the state of emergency, as the floated boliviano hit a new record Bs. 12.45/$1.
